count.av.title: In Avistry: {n} steps
count.ps.title: With Photoshop: {n} steps
count.av.1: Open Tools > Avistry > Textures and pick the avatar.
count.av.2: In the Colour tab, click the hair on the model.
count.av.4: Select Save. A new PNG and a material copy are made and put on the avatar.
count.ps.1: Find which texture the hair uses: select the mesh, open its material, find the image.
count.ps.2: Copy the PNG so the original stays safe.
count.ps.3: Export the hair's UV layout from Blender, so you know which pixels are hair.
count.ps.4: Open the PNG copy in Photoshop and place the UV layout on top as a guide.
count.ps.5: Select the hair pieces along the guide.
count.ps.6: Add a Hue/Saturation layer to the selection and shift the hue.
count.ps.7: Hide the guide and export a PNG.
count.ps.8: Back in Unity, duplicate the material.
count.ps.9: Put the new PNG in the copy's main texture slot.
count.ps.10: Put the material copy on the avatar.
count.ps.11: Check it in the Scene. If an edge or a wrong piece shows, go back to step 5.
count.note: This is one common route. Painting by eye skips the UV export but is less exact.

note.shader: Avistry saved the colours and textures. The tattoos are Avistry paint layers (ink, chrome and a bright Add layer) with a normal map made by Avistry, all saved in the texture. Glow, sparkle and the horn tint are shader values set by hand; lights, backdrop and pose are set up in Unity.

ga.honest.2: Poses are set for the photo. The arm view swings the near wing back, and the phone back view folds the wings up to fit.
ga.honest.3: The Project window picture is a real Unity window with a sample hair texture. Labels and the caption were added on top.
ga.honest.4: The tool loops are recorded in Avistry. Cursors, labels and enlarged controls are added on top, and the normal-map and Scene-bar shots use extra lights.
cu.k.face: Pick the eyes and the hair right on the model. The colour changes, the shading stays.
cu.k.arm: Glove, bangles and rings each get their own colour, all on one texture.
cu.k.wings: Stripes, frames and glow on separate layers, mixed with blend modes.
cu.k.body: Saved as a new texture and a copy of the material.
light.lead: Avistry changes the texture, not the light. The colours you pick keep their shading, so the same avatar holds up in daylight, at sunset and in a club.
